Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1033
Claimant:
Elizabeth Murillo
Adjuster:
Alison Sweeney
06/15/2025
First notice of loss received for a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection involving two vehicles. The insured
reports being stopped at a red light when a following vehicle struck the rear bumper. The driver is named on the
policy and the vehicle is covered under the current term.
07/25/2025
Contacted the claimant's attorney to confirm representation and request that all further communication be routed
through their office. The attorney has provided a letter of representation and asked that no recorded statement be
taken directly from the claimant.
08/17/2025
Reveiwed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of impact and records the other driver
as the at-fault party. Responding officers noted the vehicle positions and the damage pattern consistent with a rear
impact.
09/20/2025
Obtained photographs from the scene and from the body shop. Rear bumper, trunk lid and tail lamp damage is visible
and the damage pattern lines up well with the described force of the impact. No prior damage to this area is shown in
our records or in the photos.
10/03/2025
Spoke with the other driver, who confirms the collision occurred as described and accepts responsibility for following
too closely. The account matches what the insured reported at first notice.
10/18/2025
Two independent witnesses at the intersection gave statements that agree with the insured's account of the
sequence of events and the position of both vehicles at impact.
12/01/2025
Received medical records showing a wrist fracture diagnosed at the emergency department on the day of the
collision. The injury is consistent with the kind of force expected in this type of crash. Our records contain no prior
injury to the same body area.
12/24/2025
Claimant's attorney submitted the treatment chart. Care followed a typical course of immobilization, follow-up imaging
and physical therapy, with the frequency of visits tapering as the claimant improved and the provider noted a good
recovery.
12/26/2025
The claimant later added a few small details to the account, such as the exact position of a passenger's bag and the
timing of a phone call to the police, but the core description of the collision has remained the same across each
statement.
01/04/2026
Reviewed the vehicle's service history and prior claims. No earlier damage to the vehicle is recorded, and nohting in
the file suggests any of the current damage predates the start of coverage.
</page>

List the facts written on this page. Copy each value exactly as it is written: same spelling,
punctuation and date format. Do not add anything that is not on this page. Use "" for a missing value.

Person "role" must be one of: claimant, attorney, defense_attorney, expert, doctor, officer, adjuster, witness, other.
  claimant = the person who made the claim (also called patient, plaintiff, client, customer,
  or the driver who reported it). attorney = a lawyer for the claimant or plaintiff.
  defense_attorney = a lawyer for the insurance company or defendant.
Organization "type" must be one of: repair_shop, clinic, law_firm, court, insurer, police, other.
"policy_numbers" = only values labeled as a policy number. A claim number is not a policy number.
"street" and "city" = the person's own home address, only if the page gives it. Never use the
address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.
"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
